# Alpha's invoice again, edited — the entry description differs, so the import
# unposts and rebuilds it — and this time naming only the transaction.
#
# That transaction now carries two splits the mover could weigh: the 100.00
# Alpha's own unpost has just orphaned, and Beta's 120.00, still loose because
# Beta's invoice has not been imported. Only one of them was ever Alpha's, and
# only the mark says so — loose means unclaimed, not "belongs to whoever asks".
#
# Taking Beta's would settle this invoice out of the other customer's money and
# abandon its own settlement, with nothing ambiguous to refuse because only one
# split is loose. It would also be an overpayment of a 100.00 invoice by
# 120.00, so what a reader sees is a demand for a `prepayment:` on a payment
# they never made.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_credit_payment_block_is_checked.py.
invoice "INV-TWO-A"
	customer_id: "C-TWO-A"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-05-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-05-01
		description: "Service A, revised"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-05-02
		due: 2026-06-01
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "INV-TWO-A"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-05-15
		amount: 100
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank"
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		memo: "Portion for Alpha"
